why:
LANDED (phase-444): `nros::Node` — the Rust node handle (RFC-0022: a short-lived `&mut Executor` borrow, not an `Arc<Node>`) — now forwards this to the executor it already borrows (`nros-node/src/executor/node.rs`), over the entry point phase-381 W4 shipped on `Executor` (`executor/spin.rs`). It was verdicted `gap` — not implemented — when the capability was present one type over and only the forwarder was missing. That is the same correction phase-417 stage 2b made for `cpp:Node::*`, which is why not one `cpp:Node::*` graph row was a gap while the `rust:` ones still were.

It stays a divergence on SHAPE. rclrs returns owned heap containers (`Vec<NodeNameInfo>`, `TopicNamesAndTypes`); the graph has no bound a caller can know, so a caller-sized buffer is an unanswerable question and an owned container needs an allocator a 128 KiB target does not have. Ours streams through a visitor, which costs one entry of peak RAM; every `&str` is BORROWED for the duration of the visit and returning `false` stops the walk.

ENVELOPE (RFC-0036 §"Static CONNECTION, dynamic GRAPH"), stated in the doc comment: the call reports what has been DISCOVERED and never blocks, so an empty answer means "nobody seen yet", not "nobody exists"; a backend with no graph returns `Transport(Unsupported)`, which is a different answer from empty and must not be collapsed into zero.

**`subscription`, not `subscriber`** — rclrs's spelling, which the Rust surface takes so a porting user types what they already know. The C surface says `subscriber` because rcl does and the vtable slot says `subscriber` because upstream rmw does: three layers, three upstreams, one word each, not drift.
